chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who seizes the thief, should he raise him (to the Imam) or leave him? So he said: Indeed Safwan ibn Umayya was lying in the Sacred Mosque, so he placed down his robe and went out to pour water. He found that his robe had been stolen when he returned to it, so he said, 'Who has taken my robe?' So he went seeking it and seized the one who was with it. So he raised him to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Cut off his hand.' Safwan said: 'Will you cut off his hand for the sake of my robe, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then I gift it to him.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Why wasn't this done before you raised him to me?' I said: 'So the Imam is in his position when it is raised to him?' He said: 'Yes.' And I asked him about the pardon before it reaches the Imam, so he said: 'It is good.'

key_terms.اقْطَعُوا يَدَهُ: Cut off his hand (the penalty for theft)
key_terms.صَفْوَانُ بْنُ أُمَيَّةَ: Safwan ibn Umayya (a companion of the Prophet)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a private citizen catches a thief and wants to pardon him before taking him to the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of *al-imam bi-manzilatih* (the Imam is in the position of the Prophet) within Shia jurisprudence, specifically regarding the transition of judicial authority from the Prophet to the Imams. It clarifies that while the Prophet’s command to cut the hand was binding, the Imam retains the discretion to accept a pardon offered by the victim, even after the case has been presented to him, highlighting the flexibility in applying *hudud* penalties. The narrative of Safwan ibn Umayyah serves as a practical precedent for how private individuals can initiate and resolve criminal cases within the broader Islamic legal framework.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby,

(The narrator) says, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who seized the thief, should he raise it (the matter to the Imam<sup>asws</sup>) or should he leave him?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Sufyan Bin Amayya was lying down in the Sacred Masjid, so he placed down his robe, and went out to wash with the water. He found that his robe had been stolen, when he returned to it. So he said, ‘Who has gone away with my robe?’ So he went seeking it, and he seized the one who was with it.
So he raised it to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>. So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Cut off his hand’. So Sufyan said, ‘You<sup>saww</sup> will cut his hand due to the reason of my robe, O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>?’ He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Yes’. He said, ‘So I have gifted it to him’. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘So why didn’t you? This should have been done before you raised it to me<sup>saww</sup>’. 
I said, ‘So the Imam<sup>asws</sup> is at his<sup>saww</sup> status when it is raised to him<sup>asws</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’. And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the excusing before it ends up to the Imam<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Better’.
